lines.text: Right now, somewhere in Africa, a technician is counting malaria parasites. By hand. One by one. Against two hundred white blood cells. Field after field. Slide after slide.
It's slow. It's exhausting. And two experts can count the same slide and still disagree.
Six hundred and ten thousand people died of malaria in 2024. Tanzania ranks fourth in the world. The microscopes are there. The time isn't.
So we built Darubini. A phone on the eyepiece. A counting copilot, powered by Meta's models.
Snap a field, or just pan across the slide. Blurry? Rejected, instantly.
Hands busy? Just say it. Next field. Retake. Finish. Muse Voice Transcribe does the rest.
And Muse Spark double-checks every count before you see a report.
First, we catch every spot that takes up the stain.
Our verifier keeps only the real parasites.
And SAM 3.1 finds every white blood cell from one word. Thirty-four parasites. The expert counted thirty-five.
Panning? SAM 3.1 tracks every single cell, so nothing gets counted twice. Twelve parasites. Not thirty-one.
We trained it the right way. Split by patient, never by image. Test set locked away.
Three hundred NIH fields. Sixteen hundred Tanzanian tiles. F1 jumped from zero point two nine to zero point eight one.
Protocol frozen first. Then the test set, scored exactly once.
Then the Muse Spark agent takes over. It checks image quality, audits its own work, applies the WHO rule, and writes the report in Kiswahili.
On an unseen slide: sixteen thousand three hundred per microlitre. The expert: sixteen thousand one hundred.
The results, on patients it never saw. Parasite F1: zero point eight. Nineteen of twenty-four slides within twice the expert's density. And the audit caught every single over-count.
Every part adds accuracy. Together, they count best.
To be clear: it counts. It doesn't diagnose. A microscopist confirms every result.
And this is just the start. Tuberculosis. Schistosomiasis. Sleeping sickness. Even simulated TB cultures, to train colony counting.
Darubini. Count faster. Count once. Count with confidence.
